cards.signin: {{cast.user}} signs in to {{cast.company}} inside the app itself; PingFederate checks the password, the app never sends them anywhere.
cards.dcr: {{cast.agent}} registers itself as a new client at {{cast.company}}, but only because it holds an initial access token: without one PingFederate says no.
cards.rar: {{cast.agent}} asks to pay {{cast.payee}} a set amount, and that exact transfer, not a blanket permission, is what {{cast.user}} approves.
cards.ciba: {{cast.agent}} needs {{cast.user}}'s go-ahead while {{cast.user}} is away from the app: PingFederate asks on their own device and {{cast.agent}} waits.
cards.dpop: {{cast.agent}}'s token is bound to a key only {{cast.agent}} holds, so a copied token is worthless to anyone else.
cards.tokenExchange: {{cast.user}}'s token becomes {{cast.agent}}'s, then {{cast.serviceWord}}'s, and the final token still says who acted for whom.
cards.userinfo: {{cast.agent}} reads who {{cast.user}} is from PingFederate, with {{cast.user}}'s own access token.
cards.piflow: {{cast.company}}'s own app renders the sign-in: PingFederate answers with JSON instead of a login page.
cards.par: {{cast.agent}} hands its whole request to PingFederate first, so nothing in it can be changed on the way through the browser.
cards.pkce: Even if someone catches the code meant for {{cast.agent}}, it is useless without the secret {{cast.agent}} kept back.
